correctness.rationale: For finite chain quotient S=R/I of nilpotency length exactly 3, quotient valuation two layers have q-1 nonzero socle elements and q(q-1) valuation-one elements, each with s=|I| lifts. Layer product rule yields the complete split graph K_a∨overline(K_b), a=s(q-1), b=sq(q-1), with a>=1 and b>=2. A forcing set must and suffices to omit at most one vertex per clique/independent layer, giving u^(N-2)(u+a)(u+b), Z=M=N-2. Bilinear form H=[[0,1],[1,1]] with clique vector (0,1) and independent vector (1,0) is an exact rank-two real symmetric graph-pattern witness, and M<=Z is matching lower bound. Nonzero roots -a,-b recover q=b/a and s=a/(q-1). Independent exhaustive split-graph checks for (q,s)=(2,1),(2,2),(3,1) reproduce coefficients; symbolic valuation argument covers all q,s.

originality.rationale: Boyer et al. 2019 Theorems 10 and 12 already classify every zero forcing set and the complete polynomial for every connected threshold graph. The claimed K_a∨overline(K_b) is a threshold graph with binary construction 0^b1^a, exactly two blocks and a single 1-block. Since b>=2, Boyer Theorem 10 applies: at most one excluded vertex from each block, while the condition on two excluded 1-vertices is vacuous. This gives the exact entire claimed polynomial and all minimum sets without any new forcing theorem. A previously published exact ideal-based chain quotient reconstruction theorem also gives q,s via vertex degree classes; extracting them from polynomial root magnitudes and the rank-two bilinear matrix are routine deductions. Thus the original full research claim is covered as a corollary of stronger prior results despite not being printed with its ring-specific parameters.
residual_risks: None concerning the decisive threshold-graph implication; relevance of other less accessible ideal-based literature cannot restore the originality of the claimed forcing polynomial.
